title: Spatial data-type catalog
description: Everything the workflow knows about a specific spatial data type: how to recognise a folder of it on disk, which reader loads it, and which bundled recipes preprocess it. The workflow itself contains no data-type-specific logic — adding or changing support is an edit to data_types.json alone.

catalog_version.description: Bumped when the shape of this file changes incompatibly.

common_params.description: Analysis knobs shared across data types, exposed once as workflow parameters. Each names the recipe parameter it fills and the data types it applies to; the workflow passes it only to those types, and nextflow_schema.json lists the applicable types in the parameter's description.

enum.description: Closed set of accepted values, mirrored into nextflow_schema.json.

recipe_params.description: Recipe-level parameter name(s) this fills. More than one when a single concept is spelled differently by the recipes it feeds — the cluster column is `cluster_key` to the clustering recipe and `cell_type_key` to the neighborhood one. A recipe that declares none of them ignores the value.

applies_to.description: Data-type ids whose recipes actually declare one of `recipe_params`. Not every knob applies to every type — a targeted panel has no highly-variable-gene step, a whole-transcriptome one has no per-gene cell floor. Verified against the recipes themselves by tests/check_catalog.py, so this cannot drift, and mirrored into each parameter's description in nextflow_schema.json.

id.description: Stable identifier — what --data_types filters on and what appears in reports.

reader.description: Registry key of the read-effect function that loads this type (cli.py --parser).

reader_params.description: Extra kwargs merged into the reader call (cli.py --reader-params).

recipes.description: Bundled recipe file names under backend/app/recipes/, run back to back in one session. Empty means this type loads but has no default preprocessing.

validated.description: Whether these recipes have actually been executed against real data of this type. False is honest, not a defect — it tells a reader the defaults are reasoned rather than proven.

notes.description: Why the recipe is what it is, for a reader deciding whether to trust it.

runMetrics.description: An instrument-written summary inside the data folder, surfaced in the report next to the analysis numbers. Optional — a format that ships no such file simply omits this.

file.description: Path relative to the data folder.

format.description: csv_first_row: a header row plus one row of values, the shape both 10x and Vizgen use.

columns.description: Which columns to surface. These files carry dozens; a report showing all of them is unreadable. Columns absent from a given file version are skipped rather than erroring.

detect.description: How a folder of this type is recognised. Patterns are shell globs matched against paths relative to the candidate folder; a pattern containing '/' is matched against that subfolder's listing, so nesting stays explicit and discovery never walks a whole tree to test one folder. A folder matches when every all_of pattern matches, every any_of group has at least one match, and no none_of pattern matches.

all_of.description: Every one of these must be present.

any_of.description: Each inner group must have at least one member present — the way a format that permits alternative file names is expressed.

none_of.description: None of these may be present. This is how two types whose patterns overlap are told apart (e.g. a Visium HD run also carries Visium's count matrix, one level down).
